title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 306: The Invention of the Alphabet
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 306 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Invention of the Alphabet: Script, Statecraft, and Literacy

Paragraph 1. Thousands of years ago, ancient writing in Egypt and Mesopotamia used hundreds or even thousands of picture symbols. Each picture stood for a whole idea or a whole word. Because there were so many signs, writers had to study for decades to remember them all. Only a small group of rich priests and royal clerks could read and write. Ordinary farm workers had to ask these clerks for help whenever they needed to read laws or trade contracts.

Paragraph 2. Around 1800 BCE, a simpler kind of writing appeared far away from royal palaces. Archaeologists found early stone marks inside turquoise mines in the Sinai desert. Foreign workers in the mines did not know how to attend elite Egyptian schools. Instead, they borrowed about twenty-four Egyptian picture signs and used them to show simple spoken sounds.

Paragraph 3. This new sound alphabet changed history because it needed only about thirty letters. Any person who could speak could learn to read and write in just a few weeks. Royal kings ignored it at first and called it ugly writing by poor workers. However, Phoenician sea traders loved how fast and useful it was for business. By sailing across the sea, traders carried this alphabet to Greece and Rome, creating Greek and Latin letters.

Paragraph 4. Still, not every ancient thinker praised written alphabets. The Greek teacher Socrates warned that writing everything down on paper could make human memory lazy. He believed people might think they are wise just by reading words, without truly remembering ideas inside their minds.

q1.text: Ancient writing systems in Egypt and Mesopotamia used hundreds or thousands of symbols.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...used hundreds or even thousands of picture symbols."

q2.text: Mine workers in Sinai received gold coins as a reward for inventing new letters.

steps: Đoạn 2: Bài chỉ nói thợ mỏ tạo ra chữ cái từ hình vẽ Ai Cập, không nhắc chuyện được thưởng tiền vàng.

q3.text: Phoenician sea traders refused to use the new alphabet in their business.

steps: Đoạn 3: Thương nhân biển Phoenicia rất thích (loved how fast and useful it was) và mang đi khắp nơi.

q4.text: Socrates worried that writing words down could weaken human memory.

steps: Đoạn 4: "Socrates warned that writing everything down... could make human memory lazy."
Đoạn 1: "...study for decades to remember them all."
Đoạn 2: "...used them to show simple spoken sounds."
Đoạn 3: "...learn to read and write in just a few weeks."
